aliases: Anxi Long Juan Tie Guan Yin
processing: Made as Anxi Tie Guan Yin generally is: partial oxidation, repeated rolling into pellets and drying. No separate township method is recorded.
harvest_season: Spring and autumn, like all Anxi Tie Guan Yin.
appearance_dry: Tight green pellets, as is typical of Anxi Tie Guan Yin in the light style.
appearance_liquor: Pale yellow-green and clear, as with light Anxi Tie Guan Yin.
appearance_wet: Whole leaves unfurl, as with other Tie Guan Yin.
taste_profile: No taste specific to Longjuan is well recorded. Expect the florals and creamy body typical of light Anxi Tie Guan Yin.

brewing.notes: Treat it as a light Tie Guan Yin: rinse quickly, keep water just off the boil and keep the first steeps short.

vintage_note: Sold by season and year like other Anxi Tie Guan Yin, usually the spring or autumn of the current year. Drink the light style within about a year. Named villages can fetch more than the average, so ask which village it came from.
description:
Longjuan is a township in Inner Anxi, the mountainous western part of the county, and this is Tie Guan Yin sold under its name. It is a claim about place, not a separate kind of tea.

The method is the usual Anxi one. Inner Anxi as a whole has mountains, mist and acidic red soil, though the township has no separately documented character.

In the cup, expect the light Tie Guan Yin pattern of florals over a creamy texture, using very hot water and short steeps. Unlike Gande, Xianghua and Xiping, Longjuan has no famous slogan telling you what to look for, so you can taste it without expectations.

It appears only occasionally under its own name in export shops. Ask for the village and season, as with any Anxi tea; Nanqi is one village that a press report singled out for strong wholesale prices.
history: Little is documented about Tie Guan Yin in Longjuan specifically, beyond its place among the tea townships of Inner Anxi. A 2017 press report on the autumn season mentioned tea bases and a farmers' cooperative federation in the township, and noted wholesale prices holding up at villages such as Nanqi.
